  Effective business planning depends on accurate and consistent forecasts

# Introduction {#sec-00-introduction .unnumbered}

In today’s increasingly complex market environment, accurate demand forecasting is vital to the operational efficiency of supply chains — particularly for perishable food products, which have a limited shelf life and are highly sensitive to seasonality and promotional activities.

This study focuses on `BioBalance`, a multi-channel food company operating in the Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) industry. The company produces its own products and sources finished goods from suppliers, distributing them through various channels including retail, Out-of-Home (OOH), Health & Food Stores (HFS), discounters, and e-commerce. To support business decisions in production, procurement, and negotiations with suppliers and customers, accurate sales forecasts are required at varying levels of aggregation, tailored to each use case.

## Research Objectives

The primary objective of this research is to assess the Forecast Value Added (FVA) by establishing a minimal-resource benchmark for forecast accuracy. FVA is defined as the difference between the accuracy achieved by the business and the accuracy attainable using a robust, low-effort forecasting approach.

As a secondary objective, this study evaluates the accuracy of hierarchical forecasting techniques, which produce consistent forecasts across multiple aggregation levels — a critical requirement for cross-functional decision-making.

## Purpose of the Research

The goal of this research is to provide insight into the cost-benefit relationship of deploying additional forecasting resources. The minimal-resource benchmark serves not only as a reference point for evaluating current performance but also as a baseline target for future improvement efforts.

## Scope of the Research

`BioBalance` offers a diverse product portfolio (SKUs) across multiple geographical markets, with products varying in sales importance. To ensure a focused and meaningful analysis, this study concentrates on the top 20% of products, which together account for 80% of total sales.

While a small portion of the company’s sales (less than 10%) comes from chilled products — which have short shelf lives and are forecasted daily — the majority comes from ambient products with an shelf life of $1/2$ to $1$ year. These are forecasted in monthly buckets and form the primary focus of this research.

By narrowing the scope to high-impact ambient products, the study enables a practical and scalable analysis, while still yielding insights that are applicable across the broader product range.

## Structure of the Document

<!-- Structure of the Document, why we chose CRISP-DM, roadmap of the sections to follow -->
This research adopts the **CRISP-ML methodology** [@costa_crisp-ml_2022] as its guiding framework.

CRISP-ML (Cross-Industry Standard Process for Machine Learning) is a structured approach for designing, implementing, and communicating data science and machine learning projects. It consists of six core phases:

1.  Business Understanding
1.  Data Understanding
1.  Data Preparation
1.  Modelling
1.  Evaluation
1.  Deployment

The main body of this document includes a dedicated section for each phase. These chapters are concise, free of code, and supported by visuals and tables to enhance readability and accessibility — particularly for business stakeholders and decision-makers.

For technical readers, the Appendix provides a corresponding chapter for each phase, offering additional context, detailed analysis, and code implementations.
